### Comparing Results

We now compare logistic regression, the pruned decision tree, and the SVM on
the **same 20% test set**, using the same 0.50 classification threshold and the
same baseline (always predict "disease"). Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity,
and AUC come from each model's own section.

```{r comp-table}
# Pull the evaluation objects created in the model sections
get_row <- function(name, cm, roc_obj) {
  data.frame(
    Model       = name,
    Accuracy    = round(as.numeric(cm$overall["Accuracy"]), 3),
    Sensitivity = round(as.numeric(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]), 3),
    Specificity = round(as.numeric(cm$byClass["Specificity"]), 3),
    AUC         = round(as.numeric(auc(roc_obj)), 3)
  )
}

baseline <- data.frame(
  Model       = "Baseline (always 'disease')",
  Accuracy    = round(mean(test$HeartDisease == "1"), 3),
  Sensitivity = 1,
  Specificity = 0,
  AUC         = 0.5
)

comp_results <- rbind(
  baseline,
  get_row("Logistic Regression", log_cm,        log_roc),
  get_row("Decision Tree",       tree_cm,       tree_roc),
  get_row("SVM (linear)",        res_linear$cm, res_linear$roc),
  get_row("SVM (radial)",        res_radial$cm, res_radial$roc)
)
rownames(comp_results) <- NULL

comp_results
```

```{r comp-roc, fig.height=4.5, fig.width=6}
# Overlay all ROC curves on one plot
roc_all <- list(
  log_roc, tree_roc, res_linear$roc, res_radial$roc
)
names(roc_all) <- c(
  sprintf("Logistic (AUC = %.3f)",     auc(log_roc)),
  sprintf("Tree (AUC = %.3f)",         auc(tree_roc)),
  sprintf("SVM linear (AUC = %.3f)",   auc(res_linear$roc)),
  sprintf("SVM radial (AUC = %.3f)",   auc(res_radial$roc))
)

ggroc(roc_all, legacy.axes = TRUE, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey") +
  labs(
    title  = "ROC Curves for All Models (Test Set)",
    x      = "1 - Specificity",
    y      = "Sensitivity",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.68, 0.22))
```

```{r comp-metric-plot, fig.height=3.5, fig.width=7}
# Side-by-side bars for the four metrics (baseline excluded)
comp_long <- comp_results[comp_results$Model != "Baseline (always 'disease')", ] %>%
  pivot_longer(-Model, names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value")

ggplot(comp_long, aes(Metric, Value, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Test-set performance by model", x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r comp-confusion}
# Confusion matrices (rows = predicted, columns = actual)
list(
  "Logistic Regression" = log_cm$table,
  "Decision Tree"       = tree_cm$table,
  "SVM (linear)"        = res_linear$cm$table,
  "SVM (radial)"        = res_radial$cm$table
)
```

Are the differences in AUC real or just noise from a small test set? We use
DeLong's test to compare each model's ROC curve with logistic regression.

```{r comp-delong}
delong <- function(r1, r2, label) {
  t <- roc.test(r1, r2, method = "delong")
  data.frame(Comparison = label,
             AUC_difference = round(as.numeric(auc(r1)) - as.numeric(auc(r2)), 3),
             p_value = round(t$p.value, 3))
}

rbind(
  delong(log_roc, tree_roc,       "Logistic vs. Tree"),
  delong(log_roc, res_linear$roc, "Logistic vs. SVM (linear)"),
  delong(log_roc, res_radial$roc, "Logistic vs. SVM (radial)")
)
```

```{r comp-summary-values, include=FALSE}
# Values used in the written interpretation below
best_auc_model <- comp_results$Model[-1][which.max(comp_results$AUC[-1])]
best_acc_model <- comp_results$Model[-1][which.max(comp_results$Accuracy[-1])]
best_sens_model <- comp_results$Model[-1][which.max(comp_results$Sensitivity[-1])]
best_spec_model <- comp_results$Model[-1][which.max(comp_results$Specificity[-1])]
```

**Interpretation:** Every model beats the baseline accuracy of
`r round(100 * baseline$Accuracy, 1)`%. By AUC, the best model is
**`r best_auc_model`** (`r max(comp_results$AUC[-1])`), and by accuracy it is
**`r best_acc_model`** (`r round(100 * max(comp_results$Accuracy[-1]), 1)`%).
`r best_sens_model` catches the most patients with heart disease (sensitivity
`r max(comp_results$Sensitivity[-1])`), while `r best_spec_model` is best at
correctly clearing patients without it (specificity
`r max(comp_results$Specificity[-1])`).

<!-- EDIT THESE THREE POINTS after you knit and see the table. They are written
     as a template; keep only the ones the numbers support. -->

- **Flexibility did not obviously help.** The SVM's radial kernel and the
  tree can both capture nonlinear patterns, but if their AUC is not clearly
  higher than logistic regression's (see the DeLong p-values), the
  relationship between the predictors and heart disease is close to linear.
- **Trees are less stable.** A single pruned tree has a coarse set of
  predicted probabilities (one per leaf), so its ROC curve is steppier and its
  AUC is usually lower than the smoother models'.
- **Interpretability favors logistic regression and the tree.** Logistic
  regression gives odds ratios, and the tree gives simple if-then rules a
  clinician could follow. The SVM predicts well but does not say *which*
  variables drive the prediction.

**Recommendation:** When models perform about the same, choose the one that is
easiest to explain. Unless one model is significantly better in the table
above, logistic regression is the best choice for this project because it
matches the others' accuracy and AUC while also showing how each clinical
predictor relates to the odds of heart disease. If the goal were to miss as few
true cases as possible, we would prioritize sensitivity and could lower the
0.50 threshold for whichever model we choose.

**Limitations:** The test set is only about 184 patients, so a difference of a
few patients changes accuracy by about 0.5 percentage points. All models were
compared at one train/test split (seed 380), and the 0.50 threshold was not
tuned for any model.
